rationale: Evidence: iteration 6 (kp 3.0, ki 0.8, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, outer sensors at x = ±0.04, sensor_size 0.016, last_direction) is the best raced design at 184.93, up from 175.70 at ki 0.4. Progress on s-bend rose from 0.40 to 0.45, and the oval rose from 0.69 to 0.65 with the finish rate at 0.10 (2/20). Slalom progress was 0.1165, marginally below the 0.12 of iteration 5, so the slalom is roughly flat. Steering oscillation fell on the oval (0.33 to 0.30) and rose only slightly on the s-bend (0.33 to 0.34), still under the 0.35 threshold. Max_error is about 0.060 to 0.064 m on every track, so the residual offset is still present. The Evaluator's entityR1 feedback describes the iteration 5 design with ki 0.8, which is the iteration 6 design already raced, so I treat that feedback as stale and rely on the iteration 6 race data (R2A). Earlier evidence still holds: higher kp (iteration 4) and wider outer sensors (iteration 3) both lowered the score, so they stay fixed, and base_speed 1.2 (iteration 2) cost oval finishes. Change: raise ki from 0.8 to 1.0 with all other fields unchanged. This is the next single-variable step on the integral lever, which has improved progress on the bends at each step (0.4 to 0.8 gave +9.2). The integral is clamped to ±2, which limits windup. Expected result: s-bend progress at or above 0.45, slalom progress at or above 0.12, max_error slightly lower, and a score at or above 184.93. Watch steering_oscillation on the s-bend: if it rises above about 0.35, return ki to 0.8, the iteration 6 fallback with score 184.93. If the score falls below 184.93 with progress unchanged, keep iteration 6. Measurements wanted: per-track progress, max_error, steering_oscillation, line_loss_events, and completion_time on the oval.
